description: Daucus carota subsp. sativus: grown for its orange taproot.

diseases.name: Alternaria Leaf Blight
diseases.description: A fungal blight of carrot leaves, starting on the older leaves.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on carrot debris and seed and spread by wind and rain in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots on the leaflet edges
Leaflets shrivel; the whole top can die
diseases.effect: Weak tops break when harvesting by machine; roots stay small.
diseases.untreated: Severe blight kills the foliage and cuts yield.

steps.title: Remove blighted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off blighted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Water in the morning, at the base
Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Rotate away from carrots for 2-3 years

lifecycle: The fungus survives on debris and seed.
Wind and rain carry spores to old leaves.
Dark spots with yellow surrounds form.
Leaflets shrivel and the top blights.

diseases.name: Cavity Spot
diseases.description: A soil-borne disease that pits the carrot root with small sunken lesions.
diseases.causes: Pythium water moulds in the soil infect the root, especially in wet, compacted soils; it builds up with frequent carrot crops.
symptoms: Small, sunken, elliptical lesions across the root
Lesions grey to brown; the skin over them may crack
diseases.effect: Pitted roots cannot be sold fresh.
diseases.untreated: Losses grow the longer roots stay in the ground.

steps.title: Lift the crop on time
steps.instruction: Harvest promptly once roots size up.
steps.rationale: Lesions keep developing while roots stay in the soil.

steps.title: Improve drainage
steps.rationale: Wet soil favours the water moulds.

steps.title: Rotate fields
steps.instruction: Leave several years between carrot crops.
steps.rationale: The water moulds build up in the soil.

prevention.title: Long rotations
prevention.detail: Four or more years between carrots.

lifecycle: The water moulds live in the soil.
In wet soil they infect the root.
Small sunken lesions form across the root.
They build up with frequent carrot crops.

diseases.name: Cercospora Leaf Blight
diseases.description: A fungal leaf blight of carrot, often on younger leaves and leaf edges.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on debris and seed and spread by wind and splash in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Small tan spots with dark borders on the leaflets
diseases.untreated: Yield falls when foliage dies early.

steps.title: Remove blighted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off blighted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Keep the tops dry
steps.instruction: Water early in the day, at the base.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on debris and seed.
Spores spread in warm, humid weather.
Tan spots with dark borders form.
